blocking_issues.title: An uncommitted pending transaction permanently blocks replay of its epoch
blocking_issues.trigger: A numeric pending transaction exists, but the owner did not commit that epoch; a reviewed recovery replays it under the next physical attempt.
blocking_issues.finding: commit_snapshot uses one immutable transactions/<key>/epoch_XX.json for all physical attempts. Replayed attempt/path, commit_requested timestamp, serialization timings and usually continuation hash differ. immutable rejects the new pending transaction before commit. recover/reconcile_ack only reconcile an existing owner ACK; they never resolve a pending transaction for an epoch not present in RAM.
blocking_issues.evidence: Actual commit_snapshot invoked twice with in-memory persistence and a simulated failure before commitment. Both a valid formal E1/step20 snapshot and an engineering ordinal1/step2 snapshot reproduced Immutable receipt differs at the canonical transactions/.../epoch_01.json. No real writes or IPC.
blocking_issues.correction: Preserve each uncommitted physical transaction with attempt identity; select exactly the successful ACK-bound transaction for the canonical scientific epoch. Reconcile a committed transaction without resending it. Permit a genuinely uncommitted epoch to create its next physical transaction. Do not overwrite/drop prior failed receipts or relax continuation/hash checks.
blocking_issues.focused_acceptance: Finite failed-before-commit -> recovery -> new-attempt replay -> ACK case, plus the already-committed/lost-ACK case; all failed costs and transaction identities retained.

blocking_issues.title: Engineering technical failures cannot pass through the implemented reviewed recovery path
blocking_issues.trigger: One of the four engineering cases fails after prefix ordinal1 is acknowledged and before its final verified case receipt/signoff, or after suffix ACK but before receipt finalization.
blocking_issues.finding: smoke_case rejects every registration with an existing acknowledged state. smoke has no recovery continuation. recover requires validate_attempt(require_engineering=True), which already requires all four completed/signed/released cases, and then skips every non-formal job. The fixed case/key therefore has no implemented path to finish from its retained prefix. Re-running the same smoke command cannot clear it, and releasing it before acceptance is forbidden.
blocking_issues.evidence: Actual smoke_case invoked with an in-memory registration containing an acknowledged prefix; it deterministically rejects at line383 before Profile/GPU/IPC. Independently traced recover engineering prerequisite and its formal-only filter, and frozen serve recover/register/paused contracts.
blocking_issues.correction: Provide source/design/pause/owner-bound reviewed recovery for the existing engineering cases before engineering signoff. Reconcile their actual ACK/journal and resume the registered finite case plan from retained state, or finalize an already-verified suffix safely. Preserve physical attempt/call costs, exact source/replay checks, fixed scientific protocol, scientific_epochs=0 and all four protected engineering keys. Do not bypass the resource gate, contact old owners, fake COMPLETE50, or release an unaccepted key.
blocking_issues.focused_acceptance: Finite engineering failure after prefix ACK and after suffix ACK but before final receipt; recover without requiring the signoff being produced, retain earlier costs, and complete genuine case evidence without fabricated calls.

blocking_issues.title: Startup profiling can count live torch allocations as non-torch overhead
blocking_issues.trigger: The sampler runs while _new_objects has already allocated CUDA model/EMA tensors but has not returned.
blocking_issues.finding: Profile starts with cuda_ready=False and forces torch allocated/reserved to zero until after all _new_objects construction, device moves and EMA copy finish. NVML already includes those tensors during that interval, so own_process_bytes is recorded as non_torch_bytes. The maximum is permanent and measured_envelope later adds it to the torch-reserved peak, double-counting the misclassified allocator bytes. This is not the specified measured reserved-plus-actual-non-torch capacity envelope.
blocking_issues.evidence: Actual Profile._sample on a finite telemetry fixture with own residency900 and allocator reserved500, cuda_ready=False: reports reserved0/non_torch900 instead of non_torch400 and never queries allocator counters. Source call ordering establishes the legitimate allocation window. No actual hardware measurements were claimed.
blocking_issues.correction: Begin sampling before context creation, then enable correct allocator telemetry as soon as the process CUDA context exists and before model/EMA/optimizer allocations. Keep early context observations, phase coverage and maximum full-process measurements, but never classify torch residency as non-torch merely because initialization is in progress. Use correctly measured peaks for the existing usable-capacity fit predicate; do not add a cap, projected85% gate or guessed peak.
blocking_issues.focused_acceptance: Finite staged context/model/EMA telemetry interleaving verifies actual allocator/non-torch decomposition and envelope arithmetic. Actual four-case profiling still requires independent RUN-stage resource review.

nonblocking_issues.title: COSTS export does not expose all required diagnostic/restore cost components
nonblocking_issues.finding: COSTS contains snapshot-transfer and combined logical-epoch/validation records; returned per-batch diagnostic_seconds is left only in batch logs. restore has no separate elapsed-cost record. Required diagnostic/restore breakdown therefore cannot be read from the advertised cost table. This does not invalidate the inspected loss formulas or erase the available batch diagnostic timings.
nonblocking_issues.correction: Export existing returned diagnostic timings with their physical attempt provenance and measure restore time separately. Preserve unknown partial work as null; do not infer missing durations by subtracting unrelated totals.
